item.title: Migrating a Remix Project to Cloudflare
item.author: Author
item.description:
Migrating a Remix Project to Cloudflare

Recently I developed a project using remix. I hadn’t done full-stack development before; I’d used reactjs a bit but wasn’t very familiar with it, and I was using Nextjs, which felt very hard to use — mainly because after version 13 switched to the app router, I was somewhat at a loss.

Later I discovered remix, which uses filename-based routing directly and is much more convenient, and the loader and action approach is also very intuitive, so I chose remix.

item.title: Playing Around with ComfyUI
item.author: Author
item.description:
Playing Around with ComfyUI

AIGC was very popular a while back, so I deployed Stable Diffusion’s WebUI locally and played with it for a bit. See: text

But the WebUI interface is too complex and has too many elements. It looks very professional, but it’s also somewhat difficult to use. I happened to be busy with work around that time, so after playing with it for a while I set it aside and didn’t continue.

item.title: Deploy a Local Stable Diffusion Runtime Environment
item.author: Author
item.description:
Deploy a Local Stable Diffusion Runtime Environment

midjourney has been quite popular lately, but it has started charging—10 dollars a month, which is more than I can afford—so I switched to the open-source Stable Diffusion. You can deploy it on Google Colab with one click: https://github.com/camenduru/stable-diffusion-webui-colab. However, the free gpu on Google Colab runs out quickly, and although the paid one is cheap, you still have to use it sparingly. If you have a local gpu with more than 8G of VRAM, you can run it on your own computer to save costs; 6G of VRAM should also work—try lowering the resolution and keywords.
